title: Descent of flat families with local complete intersection geometric fibres
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and limit $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $i_0\in I$, quasi-compact quasi-separated $S_{i_0}$-schemes $U_0,V_0$, and an $S_{i_0}$-morphism $g_0:U_0\to V_0$. For $i\geq i_0$ put $U_i=U_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$, $V_i=V_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$, and let $g_i:U_i\to V_i$ be the induced morphism; define $g:U\to V$ similarly over $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume $g_0$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], $g$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ [def-weil-geometric-point] the geometric fibre $U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is a local complete intersection over $\Omega$. Here a scheme locally of finite type over a field $k$ is a local complete intersection if it admits an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras that are local complete intersections as defined in [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]; empty fibres are allowed. Then there is $i\geq i_0$ such that for every $j\geq i$, $g_j$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V_j$ the geometric fibre $U_j\times_{V_j}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is a local complete intersection over $\Omega$ in this sense.

source.place: Tag 0C3L (lemma-descend-syntomic), Situation (situation-descent-property); syntomicity expressed by flatness, local finite presentation and the geometric local-complete-intersection fibre condition, using Morphisms lemma-syntomic-locally-standard-syntomic and Tag 01UF (lemma-syntomic-flat-fibres), and Algebra lemma-lci-field-change. Persistence on a directed tail is base-change stability of syntomic morphisms.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-affine-limit-chart-family] with $X_0=U_0$, $Y_0=V_0$ and $f_0=g_0$. Obtain finitely many affine triples with fixed finitely presented maps $B_{a,0}\to C_{ab,0}$ over $R_{a,0}$, coordinate systems $R_{a,i}$, and colimits $R_a$. Retain the arrow identifications and the target and source covers at every stage and at the limit.

source.place: Tag 0C3L (lemma-descend-syntomic), first paragraph; finite affine covers as in its proof.

proof.text: The base change $g$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3). Thus the given flatness and geometric-fibre assumption give condition (1) of [lem-trf-syntomic-geometric-fibres-affine-criterion]. Its implication (1) to (2), on the affine pairs supplied by step 1, says that $R_a\otimes_{R_{a,0}}B_{a,0}\to R_a\otimes_{R_{a,0}}C_{ab,0}$ is flat and finitely presented and that every ordinary residue-field fibre is a local complete intersection. This supplies the ordinary-fibre hypothesis for ring descent.

source.place: Tags 01UD/01UE/01UF, with Algebra Tag 00SJ for the geometric formulation; Morphisms Tag 01TS for local finite presentation under base change.

proof.text: Use the tail $I_{\geq i_0}$, which is nonempty (it contains $i_0$) and directed: an upper bound in $I$ of two tail indices remains in the tail. Apply [lem-trf-syntomic-ring-filtered-colimit-descent] separately to each fixed finitely presented map from step 1 and its base-ring system on this tail. Step 1 gives its colimit $R_a$, and step 2 supplies its limit hypotheses, so obtain $k_{ab}\geq i_0$ with all three ring properties. Enumerate the finitely many pairs $(a,b)$. Starting at $i_0$, successively replace the current bound by a directed upper bound of it and the next $k_{ab}$. The final index $i$ dominates every $k_{ab}$ and $i_0$; for no source charts the starting index $i_0$ already works.

source.place: Tag 0C3L (lemma-descend-syntomic), second paragraph: apply Algebra Tag 0C33 (lemma-colimit-lci) on each affine triple.

proof.text: Fix $j\geq i$. Since $i_0\leq k_{ab}\leq i\leq j$, the compatible coordinate-ring system of step 1 supplies $R_{a,0}\to R_{a,k_{ab}}\to R_{a,j}$. Apply [lem-trf-lci-fibre-tensor-transition] to this chain and $B_{a,0}\to C_{ab,0}$. Step 3 supplies exactly its three hypotheses at $k_{ab}$; no flatness of the transition is needed. Its tensor and residue-field comparisons give flatness, finite presentation and local-complete-intersection residue-field fibres for $B_{a,j}\to C_{ab,j}$. The arrow identifications of step 1 identify this map with the restricted chart map of $g_j$.

source.place: Tag 00SN (lemma-base-change-syntomic), its three-line proof via flat base change, finite presentation base change and Tag 00SJ; tensor identifications written explicitly.

proof.text: The covers and arrow identifications of step 1 identify the chart properties of step 4 with condition (3) of [lem-trf-syntomic-geometric-fibres-affine-criterion] for $g_j$. Its implication (3) to (1) gives flatness, local finite presentation and the geometric local-complete-intersection fibre condition for every algebraically closed field. This holds for each $j\geq i$, as required; the cited criterion allows empty source covers and empty fibres.

source.place: Tag 01UD (lemma-syntomic-characterize), (4) implies (1), combined with Tags 01UE/01UF and Algebra Tag 00SJ as in the affine criterion.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0C3L (lemma-descend-syntomic), finite affine reduction and Algebra Tag 0C33; the geometric reformulation is Morphisms Tags 01UD/01UE/01UF with Algebra Tag 00SJ; directed-tail persistence is the proof of Algebra Tag 00SN.
